growth_opportunities.title: Elevate Wishlist Visibility & Prompting
growth_opportunities.description: Introduce contextual in‑product prompts (e.g., "Save for later?" after viewing) and a persistent wishlist icon to make the feature top‑of‑mind during browsing.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: A/B test a banner and a modal prompt that appears after 5 seconds of product view, measuring wishlist add‑rate and subsequent conversion.

growth_opportunities.title: Moodboard‑Style Social Save
growth_opportunities.description: Allow users to create visual collections that can be shared to Instagram/TikTok, turning the wishlist into a style inspiration board.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Launch a limited‑time "Style Board" feature for a subset of users and track engagement, shares, and eventual purchases from the board.

growth_opportunities.title: Deferred‑Purchase Triggers
growth_opportunities.description: Add a "Buy later" reminder tied to user‑specific events (salary day, birthdays) and send gentle push notifications.
growth_opportunities.recommended_experiment: Segment users who have viewed but not added items; send a personalized reminder after 3 days and measure conversion lift.

This suggests that a large segment of users (≈70%) prefers to buy instantly, reducing the perceived utility of a wishlist.
supporting_evidence: Observed pattern: "Repeated phrases such as ‘super easy’, ‘buy instantly’, and ‘always use this app’ indicate a direct‑to‑cart behavior."
Segment data: Impulse Direct‑to‑Cart Shoppers – defining behaviors include “Immediate purchase without saving items” and “Frequent praise of app speed, offers, and ease of checkout.”
Prioritized theme: "Dominant Impulse Purchase Mindset" – evidence strength: Medium.
alternative_explanations: Users may be using the wishlist internally (e.g., saving to a personal collection) but do not feel the need to mention it because the purchase flow feels seamless.
The app’s current UI may already auto‑save viewed items in a hidden list, making explicit wishlist actions unnecessary from the user’s perspective.
validated_root_causes.business_impact: Reduced activation of a high‑margin funnel (wishlist → reminder → purchase), limiting cross‑sell and upsell opportunities and potentially inflating acquisition cost per order.
validated_root_causes.customer_impact: While impulse shoppers enjoy fast checkout, they miss out on benefits of planned purchasing such as better budgeting, outfit coordination, or access to future promotions tied to saved items.

active_problem_statement:
You are an expert NLP Data Analyst specializing in E-commerce Growth and Consumer Psychology. Your sole mission is to process raw scraped reviews and extract precise human motivations behind two behaviors:
1. WISHLIST INTENT (Why users add items to a wishlist instead of buying)
2. NON-MONETARY DROP-OFF (Why users leave items in a wishlist without purchasing, excluding discounts/price issues)

---
### INSTRUCTIONS:
Process each review strictly through the following classification framework. Ignore all generic feedback, post-purchase shipping complaints, app crashes, or payment failure bugs. Focus ONLY on pre-purchase hesitation and saving psychology.

1. CLASSIFY INTENT (Select one if present):
   - [MOODBOARD]: Saving for style inspiration, aesthetic matching, or social media outfit ideas (Reels/TikTok/Instagram).
   - [DEFERRED_PURCHASE]: Intending to buy later (salary delay, occasion planning, waiting to buy multiple items together).
   - [COMPARISON]: Saving to compare against alternative fits, brands, or platforms later.

2. CLASSIFY DROP-OFF FRICTION (Select one if present - NON-MONETARY ONLY):
   - [FIT_UNCERTAINTY]: Lack of confidence in sizing, real-life fabric quality, or how it looks on real body types.
   - [TREND_DECAY]: Loss of interest over time, trend expired, or realization that it was an impulse save.
   - [WISHLIST_CLUTTER]: The saved list became too large, disorganized, or overwhelming to review.
   - [STOCK_SENSITIVITY]: Size went out of stock before decision was made, leading to abandonment.

3. NOISE FILTERING RULE:
   - If a review mentions "refund", "delivery boy", "damaged package", "app crash", "OTP", or contains fewer than 4 meaningful words, MARK AS: [FILTERED_OUT].
